observation: A meta-analysis of 319 studies (Kofler et al.) finds ADHD's core marker is higher within-person (moment-to-moment) reaction-time variability, considered by some researchers more diagnostic than mean-level slowness.
claim: Riemann should design for a moving baseline rather than a fixed user profile — capacity fluctuates within and across sessions, not just between users.
mechanism: ADHD attention regulation is intrinsically noisier moment-to-moment, not just uniformly slower.

implications.text: Every session/document open should default to a safe floor (L0 or last-used level) rather than assuming yesterday's good session predicts today.

observation: Eysenck & Derakshan's Attentional Control Theory: anxiety specifically impairs central-executive inhibition/shifting functions, while sleep loss impairs sustained attention/working memory broadly — different mechanisms, and anxiety can preserve output quality at the cost of efficiency (more effort for the same result).
claim: Load capacity and emotional state (anxiety) are separate, independently-fluctuating signals that should drive different UI responses, not one collapsed 'bad day' flag.
mechanism: Anxiety specifically taxes inhibition/switching; fatigue/sleep loss taxes broad sustained attention and working memory — the same UI response ('simplify') is miscalibrated for the anxious-but-capable case.

implications.text: Model capacity (energy/attention bandwidth) and affect (anxious/calm) as two independent axes; an anxious-but-capable state should reduce choice/switching demands, not content volume.

observation: Altmann & Trafton's goal-activation model and empirical interruption studies show a brief interruption lag with time to prospectively encode/rehearse the current goal sharply reduces resumption cost versus no lag.
claim: A one-tap 'leaving now' capture of where the user was (auto-suggested from the anchored node) is directly justified as a prospective-encoding moment, not just a nice-to-have.
mechanism: Rehearsing the goal just before suspension slows the decay of that goal's activation, speeding later re-retrieval.
population: general adults (converging cognitive-psychology and applied HCI studies)

implications.text: Offer (never force) a one-tap 'state bookmark' on close/switch-away, auto-suggested from the anchored node plus one optional word, as the prospective-encoding moment the research supports.

observation: A 2025 meta-analysis found no reliable memory advantage for unfinished vs. completed tasks (classic Zeigarnik effect on recall), but did find a more robust general tendency to spontaneously want to resume interrupted tasks (Ovsiankina effect).
claim: Don't build a feature that assumes 'leaving something unfinished helps you remember it' (weak evidence); do build on 'you'll feel pulled to come back to it' (better-evidenced), e.g. a visible but non-urgent unfinished-reading tray.
mechanism: The Zeigarnik memory-enhancement claim and the Ovsiankina resumption-pull claim are often conflated in pop-science, but only the pull-to-resume effect replicates well.
context: meta-analysis; primary text access was blocked, relying on secondary summary

implications.text: Build a lightweight, visible-but-not-urgent unfinished-reading tray on the pull-to-resume mechanism, not on a claimed memory-enhancement effect.

observation: Streak-mechanic complaints (asymmetric loss framing, all-or-nothing reset clashing with ADHD's inconsistency) are documented in practitioner/blog sources, not peer-reviewed studies, though the underlying loss-aversion mechanism (losses ~2x as motivating as gains) is well-established behavioral economics.
claim: No streaks; if any continuity mechanic exists, it should be non-resettable and proportional (e.g. a rolling 7-day engaged-days count) rather than an all-or-nothing chain.
mechanism: Streak mechanics are structurally loss-averse; a single miss triggers a full reset, which specifically clashes with ADHD's day-to-day performance inconsistency.

implications.text: Never implement streak mechanics; if a continuity indicator exists, make it non-resettable and proportional.

observation: Gollwitzer & Sheeran's 2006 meta-analysis (94 independent tests, >8,000 participants) found implementation intentions ('if situation Y, then I will do X') have a medium-to-large effect on goal attainment, d≈.65.
claim: Riemann should let users set implementation-intention-style defaults ('if it's after 9pm, open at L1') rather than relying purely on real-time inferred state, since inference accuracy is currently weak.
mechanism: Implementation intentions work by increasing accessibility of the trigger situation and automating the response, independent of momentary willpower.
population: general adults (large meta-analysis across many behavior-change domains)

implications.text: Offer a one-time, low-friction implementation-intention setup ('if X then default to level Y') rather than betting purely on real-time state inference.

observation: Gruber, Gelman & Ranganath (2014, Neuron) found curious states activate dopaminergic reward circuitry and enhance hippocampal memory not just for the curiosity-triggering content but for incidental information encountered during the curious state.
claim: L0 gists phrased as bounded questions/gaps ('the surprising reason X happened') rather than flat statements may recruit more curiosity-driven engagement and improve incidental retention of surrounding L1/L2 content.
mechanism: Curiosity triggered by a known, bounded information gap activates reward circuitry that broadly enhances memory encoding, not just for the gap's answer.

implications.text: Test an L0 phrasing style that poses a bounded question/gap rather than only stating the compressed fact, as an opt-in variant worth A/B testing.

observation: Wendy Wood's research program finds ~43% of daily behavior is habitual, activated by recurring context cues (place, preceding action) and relatively insensitive to short-term goal/motivation changes; moving to a new context breaks habitual autopilot.
claim: A consistent, unchanging 'home' anchor builds habit automaticity over time; the anchor's consistency — not its cleverness — is what eventually makes opening Riemann effortless.
mechanism: Habits bind to stable context cues; churn in the entry point disrupts habit formation independent of how good the new design is.

implications.text: Protect the home anchor from redesign churn even as new features are added; attach novelty to peripheral regions, not the anchor itself.
